2. Mr. Dinesh Chauhan and Mr.
Pramod Tiwari, learned A.G.A. for the
State.
3. By means of the present
applications, the applicants seek
anticipatory bail in connection with Case
Crime/F.I.R. No. 0190 of 2026 dated
24.05.2026, registered under Sections
318(4), 336(3), 338, 340(2) and 61(2) of
the B.N.S. at Police Station Kotwali,
District Dehradun.
4. Both the anticipatory bail
applications arise out of the same F.I.R.;
therefore, they are heard and decided
together by this common order.

UKHC010099962026
2026:UHC:9180
4. Learned counsel for the applicants
would submit that the impugned F.I.R.
has been lodged alleging therewith that
the complainant had purchased a
property through a registered sale deed
and subsequently discovered that the
same property had also been sold to
certain other persons; that, the only
allegation against the present applicant
is that she is the daughter-in-law of one
Rituraj, who is stated to have executed
the sale deed in question. It is further
alleged that, being a schoolmate of the
complainant's son, the applicant along
with her husband had merely introduced
the complainant's son to the said
Rituraj; that, except for the aforesaid
allegation, no specific role has been
assigned to the applicant in the alleged
transaction and, even if the allegations
contained in the F.I.R. are taken at their
face value, no offence is made out
against her.
5. Learned State Counsel would
submit that the investigation has been
completed and the charge-sheet has
already been submitted before the
competent court.
6. Learned counsel for the applicants
would further submit that this Court,
vide orders dated 10.06.2026 and
12.06.2026, had granted interim
protection from arrest to the applicants;
that, pursuant thereto, the applicants
have remained available to the
Investigating Officer and have extended
full cooperation during the course of
investigation. It is further submitted that
the investigation having culminated in
filing of the charge-sheet, no further

UKHC010099962026
2026:UHC:9180
custodial interrogation of the applicants
are warranted. Learned counsel,
therefore, prays that the interim
anticipatory bail granted to the applicant
on 10.06.2026 and 12.06.2026 be made
absolute.
7. Having heard learned counsel for
the parties and upon perusal of the
material available on record, this Court
finds that the applicants have remained
protected from arrest pursuant to the
interim orders dated 10.06.2026 and
12.06.2026 and there is nothing on
record to indicate that the applicants
have misused the liberty so granted or
have failed to cooperate with the
investigation. The investigation has
already been concluded and the charge-sheet has been submitted before the
competent court. The matter has,
therefore, progressed beyond the stage of
investigation, and no material has been
brought on record to demonstrate that
the custodial interrogations of the
applicants are presently necessary.
8. It is also a relevant consideration
that the applicants have remained under
the protection of this Court for a
considerable period and has, pursuant
to the interim order, subjected
themselves to the process of
investigation. In the absence of any
material indicating misuse of the interim
protection, interference with the liberty
already extended to the applicants at
this stage would not be warranted.
Needless to observe, the observations
made herein are confined to the
consideration of the present anticipatory
bail application and shall not be

UKHC010099962026
2026:UHC:9180
construed as an expression of opinion on
the merits of the prosecution case.
9. In view of the foregoing discussion
and having regard to the overall facts
and circumstances of the case, this
Court is of the considered opinion that
the interim protection granted to the
applicants vide orders dated 10.06.2026
and 12.06.2026 deserves to be
confirmed.
10. Accordingly, the interim
anticipatory bail granted to the applicant
vide orders dated 10.06.2026 and
12.06.2026 are hereby made absolute. In
the event of arrest, the applicants shall
be released on anticipatory bail on the
same terms and conditions as contained
in the orders dated 10.06.2026 and
12.06.2026. The applicants shall
continue to abide by all such terms and
conditions and shall also remain subject
to any further condition that may be
imposed by the trial court in accordance
with law.
11. Accordingly, the anticipatory bail
applications are allowed.
12. It is clarified that none of the
observations made in this order shall
prejudice the case of either party before
the trial court, which shall decide the
case strictly on the basis of the evidence
brought on record and in accordance
with law.
13. Pending application(s), if any, also
stand disposed of.
(Alok Mahra, J.)
